# sherpa-nav

The primary application navigation rail.

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Category | nav |
| Figma | Primary Navigation |
| Source | [.ts](../../src/components/sherpa-nav/sherpa-nav.ts) · [.html](../../src/components/sherpa-nav/sherpa-nav.html) · [.css](../../src/components/sherpa-nav/sherpa-nav.css) · [.component.json](../../src/components/sherpa-nav/sherpa-nav.component.json) · [.example.json](../../src/components/sherpa-nav/sherpa-nav.example.json) |

## When to use it

For the app's side navigation rail, filled by `populate()`: an entry with `children` is an Area and never navigates, and one with an `href` is a Context. For a nav built by hand, use `sherpa-nav-item` rows.

## Example

```html
<div style="block-size: 480px"><sherpa-nav data-current-id="home"></sherpa-nav></div>
```

`populate()` is given, on `sherpa-nav`:

```json
{
  "product": {
    "name": "Sherpa"
  },
  "sections": [
    {
      "label": "Main",
      "items": [
        {
          "id": "home",
          "label": "Home",
          "icon": "home",
          "href": "?context=home"
        },
        {
          "id": "records",
          "label": "Records",
          "icon": "table-columns",
          "href": "?context=records"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "label": "Admin",
      "items": [
        {
          "id": "team",
          "label": "Team",
          "icon": "person",
          "children": [
            {
              "id": "roles",
              "label": "Roles",
              "href": "?context=roles"
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data-current-id` | text |  | id of the current Context |
| `data-menu` | boolean |  | the PHONE's menu: the whole screen, no Pin, Settings at the bottom, and Cancel — openMenu() / closeMenu() |
| `data-nav-state` | `collapsed` `hover` `default` `pinned` `settings` | `collapsed` | collapsed \| hover \| default \| pinned \| settings |
| `data-searchable` | boolean |  | show the search field (auto-set when a product is given) |

## Properties

| Property | Type | Access | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `state` | `NavState` | read and write |  |
| `pinned` | `boolean` | read and write |  |
| `activeEntry` | `NavRowInfo \| null` | read only |  |
| `currentId` | `string` | read and write |  |
| `expandedIds` | `string[]` | read only |  |

## Methods

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| `openMenu()` | openMenu() — the PHONE's menu: the nav over the whole screen, open, with no Pin; Settings at the bottom and Cancel. A Context row closes it as it goes. |
| `closeMenu()` | closeMenu() — back to the rail, going nowhere. Settings stays open. |
| `entry(id: string)` | What a row shows. Read off the stamped ROW, so hand-authored rows work too. |

## Events

Each one bubbles.

| Event | Detail | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| `nav-select` | `{ id: string }` |  |
| `nav-search` | `{ query: '' \| string }` |  |
| `nav-state-change` | `{ state: NavState }` |  |
| `nav-menu-change` | `{ open: false \| true }` | The phone's menu opened or closed |

## Slots

| Slot | Accepts | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| `icon` | icon | the product mark inside the 40×40 branding tile |
| `actions` | control | more header buttons, after Settings and Pin |
| (default) | item |  |
| `footer` | content | pinned footer content (account / user) |

## Parts

Style these from outside with `::part()`:

`actions`, `brand`, `brand-icon`, `content`, `footer`, `header`, `menu-foot`, `pin`, `product`, `quick`, `quick-zone`, `rail`, `search`, `search-clear`, `search-input`, `section-label`, `settings`
